problem: Suppose that a matrix $B$ has characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda )=(\lambda +\sqrt{2})^{3}(\lambda -2)^{21},$ the rank of $(B-2I)^{6}$ equals $4,$ and the rank of $(B-2I)^{5}$ equals $7.$ If a basis of ${R}^{24}$ consists of linearly independent generalized eigenvectors of $B$, how many of these are generalized eigenvectors of rank $6$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that a matrix $B$ has characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda )=(2-\lambda )^{3}(\lambda +\pi )^{15}(\lambda -1)^{4},$ the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{4}$ equals $8,$ and the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{3}$ equals $10.$ If a basis of ${R}^{22}$ consists of linearly independent generalized eigenvectors of $B$, how many of these are generalized eigenvectors of rank $4$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-\pi ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $B$ with eigenvalue $\lambda =-\pi ,$ a generalized eigenvector of rank $4$ is a vector $v$ such that 

$$
(B+\pi I)^{4}v=0\,\text{and}\,(B+\pi I)^{3}v\ne 0.
$$

Notice that $B$ must be a $22\times 22$ matrix.

- Since the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{3}$ equals $10,$ then by the rank-nullity theorem, we have that

$$
\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{3}=22-10=12.
$$

So, the solutions to $(B+\pi I)^{3}v=0$ form a subspace $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{3}$ of dimension $12$ in ${R}^{22}.$

- Since the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{4}$ equals $8,$  then by the rank-nullity theorem, we have that

$$
\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{4}=22-8=14.
$$

So, the solutions to $(B+\pi I)^{4}v=0$ form a subspace $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{4}$ of dimension $14$ in ${R}^{22}.$

Since $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{3}$ is a subspace of dimension $12$ in $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{4}$, which is a subspace of dimension $14,$ our basis can contain only $2$ vectors that lie in $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{4}$ but do not lie in $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{3}.$

Therefore, there will be 

$$
\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{4}-\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{3}=14-12=2
$$

 generalized eigenvectors of rank $4$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-\pi .$
